title: Historian
preamble:
This idea was captured in Minder and is ready for your consideration.

Origin: http://localhost:5001/library/idea-20260330201515
Captured: 2026-03-30
Delivered: 2026-03-30

Why this matters: Without Historian, every session starts cold. Advisors like Lug Advisor explicitly depend on Historian to source deferred or incomplete work. QA Guardian uses Historian to validate that specifications still hold. Context continuity across sessions is a core WAI value — Historian is the spoke that owns it.

Please read the brief below. Decide whether to action it, integrate it into
existing work, or defer with a note on why.
content: A spoke advisor with a focused mission to track, recall, and surface session history. Knows what was discussed, what was incompletely implemented, what was skipped, and why. Provides historical context to other advisors — particularly Lug Advisor and QA Guardian — so they can pick up where things left off without starting from scratch.
goal: Give every spoke a reliable memory of its own past. Surface incomplete and skipped work. Answer the question: what did we try, what did we decide, and what did we defer?
scope: Session history ingestion from WAI tracks. Incomplete work detection. Skipped lug tracking. Cross-advisor context supply (answers queries from Lug Advisor, QA Guardian, etc.). Validates that specifications still match implementation.
constraints: Reads from WAI track files and WAI-Lugs.jsonl. Read-only — does not modify history, only indexes and surfaces it. Must handle missing or partial track data gracefully.
why_bother: Without Historian, every session starts cold. Advisors like Lug Advisor explicitly depend on Historian to source deferred or incomplete work. QA Guardian uses Historian to validate that specifications still hold. Context continuity across sessions is a core WAI value — Historian is the spoke that owns it.

_behavior_directive.what_to_do: Review this idea in the context of the project. If it fits, scope it and plan implementation. If not, note why and mark it deferred.

intake_conversation.content: Hey! Tell me about the idea — what is it for and why does it matter?
Got it — a Historian advisor. What should it do and why does the spoke need it?

It tracks session history, knows what was discussed, what was incompletely implemented, what was skipped and why. Other advisors like Lug Advisor and QA Guardian explicitly depend on it for historical context.
So it owns the spoke memory — read-only, ingests WAI tracks, and answers history queries from other advisors. Should it also validate that specs still match current implementation?
Yes, that is the core validation responsibility — it is as important as a historian validating sources.
